gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the three enclosed printers it compares use three different kinds of 'chamber heating'. The QIDI Q2 ($449 at qidi3d.com today) has its own 280 W PTC chamber heater rated to 65 °C. Bambu Lab's P2S, which ChatGPT showed at the same $449, has no active chamber heater and only switches airflow with a flap. The Prusa CORE One's 55 °C chamber figure comes from fan/vent control with no heater named.
standout_why: I compared against the two pages ChatGPT cited and the top uncited result. goodprints3d.com (cited) gives no chamber figure or heating method for any printer and sends readers to maker pages for the P2S and CORE One+. 3dprinterlab.net (cited) says the P1S enclosure 'is not a heated chamber' and the X2D is 'actively heated (up to 65°C)', but it says nothing about the P2S, CORE One+ or QIDI Q2, and it rejects the QIDI Plus5 without giving specs. speakcad.com (rank 1, not cited) calls the CORE One 'a passive chamber to about 55 °C held by a controlled exhaust fan' and gives 60–65 °C heated figures for the QIDI Q1 Pro and Bambu H2D, but it covers neither the P2S nor the Q2. None of them lines up heater, no-heater and fan-controlled chambers at the $449 price ChatGPT recommended. None notes that Polymaker's printer wiki calls the P2S 'actively heated, up to 60' while the P2S FAQ that Welectron reproduces says it has no active chamber heating.
decides: This confirms the P2S for PLA, PETG and ABS/ASA. It challenges the P2S as the 'best all-around' pick for buyers who plan to print nylon, PA-CF or PC parts, the materials ChatGPT's own table lists for tough mechanical parts. At the same $449, the QIDI Q2 adds a dedicated 280 W chamber heater rated to 65 °C, a 370 °C hotend and a bimetal hardened-steel nozzle. The CORE One+ costs more than twice as much, and its 55 °C chamber is reached without a named heater. For engineering-polymer parts on a budget of about $500, the Q2 (which Dealectric lists, awin:qidi) is the better-matched pick. For PETG/ASA brackets and housings, the P2S stays the pick.

findings.label: Chamber heating method
findings.value: No active chamber heater; chamber temperature is managed by the closed enclosure plus an automatic flap that switches between internal and external air circulation
findings.note: This comes from the P2S FAQ section on the retailer page: 'The P2S does not have an active chamber heating function.' The same page's multi-model spec table is misaligned and shows a 65 °C 'Active Heated Chamber' value that is not clearly tied to the P2S, so I left that value out.

findings.label: Conflicting third-party chamber spec
findings.value: Polymaker lists the P2S as 'Yes, actively heated', max ambient chamber 'Up to 60' °C, and lists the P1S and X1C as 'passive heated, ~50' and the H2D as 'actively heated, 65'
findings.note: This contradicts the P2S FAQ above, which says there is no active chamber heating. It is the footnote for the table: a filament maker's guide labels the P2S as heated when the printer has no chamber heater.

findings.product: Prusa CORE One (CORE One+ shares the chassis)

findings.value: 55 °C, 'dual fans for active temperature control'; no heater named

findings.value: 'a passive chamber to about 55 °C held by a controlled exhaust fan'

findings.label: Maker's fix when the chamber fails to reach target (error #31259)
findings.value: Lower the back-panel chamber fan (Tune → Chamber fan, down to 0%) and close the top vent
findings.source_title: Failed to reach chamber temperature (#31259) – Prusa Knowledge Base
findings.note: Every fix Prusa lists reduces airflow. None turns up a heater. The article does not say what heats the chamber.

findings.label: Chamber heating (per cited rival)
findings.value: 'actively heated chamber (up to 65°C)'; hardened-steel nozzle and extruder gear; 300 °C nozzle
findings.source_title: Best 3D Printers for Durable Prints and Functional Parts (2026) – 3DPrinterLab
findings.note: This rival page was cited in ChatGPT's answer. It covers the X2D and says the P1S 'is not a heated chamber', but it has no P2S, CORE One+ or Q2 entry.
